author: League of Nations, Commission of Enquiry
title: Appeal by the Chinese Government: Report of the Commission of Enquiry (the Lytton Report)
edition: Official No. C.663.M.320.1932.VII; signed at Peiping 4 September 1932, circulated 1 October 1932
notes: The document at the centre of the pack that opens this arc. ADR 0019 makes the case for beginning at Mukden on 18 September 1931 because the Pacific war carries the cleanest demonstration of a causal chain the project has: the railway, the conquest, the League's finding, Japan's departure, and nothing done. This is the finding. Chapter IV is 'Narrative of Events in Manchuria on and Subsequent to September 18th, 1931' and Chapter V is Shanghai; the numbering above is the League's own document number, read off the Secretary-General's covering note in the scan. Quote it as a Document with the original wording, in the manner of §7 of docs/sources.md, rather than paraphrasing what the Commission concluded — the wording is the point. The scan above is open and in English.
